title: Alteration neighbourhoods regular above a prescribed quasi-excellent closed fibre
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\mathfrak q\subseteq B$ a prime ideal, and $J\subseteq B$ an ideal. Assume $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is excellent and $B/J$ is quasi-excellent [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-exc-excellent-ring]. Then there are $b\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ and finitely many integral Noetherian schemes $X_i$ with dominant generically finite morphisms $\varphi_i:X_i\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/b]$ of finite type [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], such that each local ring at a point of $\varphi_i^{-1}V(JB[1/b])$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Dominant means dense image, and generically finite means a finite extension of function fields. In addition there is an integral Noetherian scheme $V$, a proper surjective generically finite morphism $p:V\to Y$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], an open cover $V=\bigcup_i V_i$, and $Y$-morphisms $V_i\to X_i$.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Lemma 4.4 and Definition 3.2, printed pp.3,5–6; specialization with excellent B_q and quasi-excellent B/J; obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).

proof.text: Excellence of $B_{\mathfrak q}$ includes quasi-excellence by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Apply [lem-per-qe-weak-uniformization-cover] to the nonempty integral scheme $S=\operatorname{Spec}B_{\mathfrak q}$. Obtain regular integral charts $T_i\to S$ and an integral proper-surjective generically finite witness $P\to S$ with its indexed open cover and maps.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, first proof paragraph; Definition 3.2 and Theorem 3.3

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-local-alteration-diagram-spreading] to that whole diagram. Write $a\notin\mathfrak q$, $Y_a=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/a]$, and $f_i:T_{a,i}\to Y_a$ for the resulting models. All integral, finite-type, generic-field and covering-witness conditions already hold, but regularity away from $S$ has not been asserted.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, first proof paragraph, the choice of tilde b

proof.text: If $t\in T_{a,i}$ maps to a prime $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak q$, it survives the base change to $B_{\mathfrak q}$. On an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}C$ containing $t$, with prime $\mathfrak p$, every element of $B\setminus\mathfrak q$ lies outside $\mathfrak p$. Thus localization by these elements followed by localization at $\mathfrak p$ gives exactly $C_{\mathfrak p}$: those elements were already units there. The corresponding local ring on the regular scheme $T_i$ equals $\mathcal O_{T_{a,i},t}$. Consequently this ambient local ring is regular.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, equation (4.3), with the affine localization argument expanded

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-j2-closed-fibre-regular-locus] to $T_{a,i}\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $J$. This map is finite type, since $B[1/a]=B[u]/(au-1)$, and $B/J$ is J-2 by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Hence $W_i=f_i^{-1}V(JB[1/a])\setminus\operatorname{Reg}(T_{a,i})$ is closed. It is constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset], since $T_{a,i}$ is Noetherian. The affine local presentations of $f_i$ are finite presentations by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]; the Noetherian source is quasi-separated, so $f_i$ is quasi-compact and locally finitely presented. Chevalley [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image] now makes $E_i=f_i(W_i)$ constructible in the affine target $Y_a$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, definition of W and application of Lemma 4.2 and Chevalley

proof.text: The affine target $Y_a$ is spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. If $\mathfrak qB[1/a]\in\overline{E_i}$, [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-proconstructible-closure-specialization], applied to the one-member family $E_i$, gives $e\in E_i$ generalizing $\mathfrak q$. Choose $t\in W_i$ over $e$. Its image in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is a prime contained in $\mathfrak q$, so Step 3 makes its local ring regular, contradicting $t\in W_i$. Thus $\mathfrak q$ avoids every $\overline{E_i}$. Their finite union has an open complement containing $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, constructible image closure and contradiction to (4.3)

proof.text: Choose a basic neighbourhood $D(b)\subseteq D(a)\setminus\bigcup_i\overline{E_i}$ of $\mathfrak q$; explicitly choose $D(c)$ inside that open in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and set $b=ac$. Then $b\notin\mathfrak q$. Restrict the model diagram to $D(b)$. By the permanence clause of [lem-per-local-alteration-diagram-spreading] it retains every structural and witness condition. Any point above $V(JB[1/b])$ with a nonregular local ring would belong to some $W_i$ and map into $E_i\cap D(b)$, which is empty. Open restriction leaves local rings unchanged. These restricted charts and witness are the required $X_i,V,V_i$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4, final shrink and the computation W_b,i = W_a,i intersect X_b,i

proof_origin.place: Lemma 4.4, printed pp.5–6; source read online but not archived in literature. Its argument is expanded in Steps 1–6.

split_report.summary: Read Kurano–Shimomoto Lemma 4.4, Lemma 4.2/Claim 4.3 and Definition 3.2 online, and ILO VII 1.1 / II 3.2.1 in the archived volume. Split into regular local alteration cover, spreading the whole witness diagram, the ambient regular locus along the J-2 fibre, Chevalley and closure-by-specialization, and a principal shrink. Three statement-only lemmas; no Mathlib matches. Kept the statement unchanged; corrected stale bibliographic claim that a source PDF was in this sandbox.

tool_uses.why: Chevalley gives constructibility of the bad-locus image; a generic scheme-theoretic tool, not a replacement for the unit route.
Noetherian finite-type affine presentations are finite presentations, needed to apply Chevalley.
The affine target is spectral, as needed for the closure-specialization tool.
A closure point of a constructible image specializes from that image; used to exclude q from each bad-image closure.

ILO VII Thm 1.1 and II Thm 3.2.1 (ℓ=1, Zariski normal form, Y integral and proper surjective) support lem-per-qe-weak-uniformization-cover. Regular connected means integral, and alt objects are dominant and generically finite. Same-index Tᵢ/Pᵢ is fine with a repeated family. Kurano–Shimomoto is not archived (WANTED). I checked lem-per-j2-closed-fibre-regular-locus independently (Nagata criterion on Z; k[e]/e² case gives ∅) and lem-per-local-alteration-diagram-spreading by the limit argument (01ZM/081F/07RR, integral closure models, flat monomorphism base change, cover by constructible-image shrink, permanence on D(b)). Steps: S1 excellent⇒QE, so weak uniformization applies to Spec B_q. S2 spreading hypotheses hold. S3 the local-ring equality is elementary. S4 J-2 node with A=B, I=J, finite type over B; closed ⇒ constructible on a Noetherian space; Chevalley via finite type (includes quasi-compact) plus Noetherian finite presentation, affine target. S5 spectral plus closure-specialization; a generalization of q gives a contradiction via S3. S6 D(c) and b=ac, permanence, empty Eᵢ∩D(b). No duplicates: the existing alteration nodes need ℓ invertible or give étale covers; the spreading and J-2 neighbours differ. No new node restates the item.
